findings.antecedent: Granö's qualitative classification of acoustic phenomena (1929)
findings.consequent: cartographic representation of soundscapes, classifying sounds/noises by time, frequency, and natural/artificial dichotomy
findings.source: Soundscape Studies and soundmaps: a brief history, p. 3
findings.quote: The Finnish geographer made a qualitative classification of acoustic phenomena and tried to represent them cartographically. The analysis was tested in the Valoosari area and the collected material was classified in an interesting legend that indistinctly described and ordered sounds and noises according to the following criteria: time, frequency, and dichotomy between natural and artificial.

findings.consequent: analysis of soundscape by 'identity' (singularity, informativeness) and 'delightfulness' of sounds
findings.source: Soundscape Studies and soundmaps: a brief history, p. 3
findings.quote: First, he evaluated the “identity” of sounds, considering both the “singularity" of the sounds emitted and the “informativeness” of the sounds, exploring their capability in communicating activities taking place and the spatial form of a determined area. Second, he analyzed the “delightfulness” of sounds, that is to say those qualities that cause one to consider a sound more or less acceptable.

findings.consequent: evaluation of the relationship between visual and auditory perception to understand how physicality and spatial form affect the identity and appreciation of a soundscape and the perception of a city's form
findings.source: Soundscape Studies and soundmaps: a brief history, p. 3-4
findings.quote: In addition, Southworth evaluated the relationship between visual and auditory perception to understand how physicality and spatial form affects the identity and appreciation of a particular soundscape and, alternatively, how sounds affect the perception of a city's form².

findings.consequent: quantitative data (dominant height in sound signal) determines qualitative effects
findings.quote: the pitch map is particularly interesting because it constitutes the example of a case in which the analysis of the quantitative data (the determination of the dominant height in a complex sound signal, expressible in Hertz) determines, according to this interpretation, qualitative effects.

findings.consequent: investigation of relationships between soundscape and emotional dimensions related to listening to drones
findings.quote: Finally, the analysis of pitch allows to investigate possible relationships between soundscape and emotional dimensions related to listening to certain voluntary or involuntary drones, whether tuned or partially tuned (Zorzanello, 2011).

findings.antecedent: digital technology, interactive platforms and territorial GPS detection systems
findings.consequent: significant revolution in developing sound maps
findings.quote: In the past decades, digital technology, interactive platforms and territorial GPS detection systems⁵, permitted a significant revolution in developing sound maps.

findings.consequent: capable of describing sound, space, time, and social and emotional factors related to everyday life
findings.quote: Unlike traditional cartography methods that rely on static and two-dimensional reality, the soundmap is capable of describing, through sound, space and time the dimensions, and the social and emotional factors related to everyday life.

findings.consequent: conveying information about visual, spatial, acoustic and temporal aspects of a specific place, representing the soundscape through an interactive interface
findings.quote: Nowadays, a soundmap can be considered a form of “locative media”⁶, conveying information about the visual, spatial, acoustic and temporal aspects of a specific place, aimed at representing the soundscape through the use of an interactive interface.

findings.consequent: categorization as a deferred and static telematics soundmap
findings.quote: The 'tender' soundmap of Florence belongs to the deferred and static telematics soundmaps category⁷.

findings.consequent: investigation of possible relationships between Florentine soundscapes and emotional dimensions perceived by city users of Florence
findings.quote: It does not pretend to represent completely the Florentine soundscape: rather it has been drawn in order to investigate possible relationships between Florentine soundscapes and emotional dimensions perceived by city users of Florence.

findings.consequent: understanding soundscape as 'simultaneously a physical environment and a way of perceiving that environment', including an emotional and mnemonic landscape
findings.quote: it refers to a qualitative definition of soundscape that means 'simultaneously a physical environment and a way of perceiving that environment'(Thompson, 2002); something that is not only outside of us - as we are used to thinking about in our visually oriented culture - but it also includes a landscape part, in the metaphorical sense, as an emotional and mnemonic landscape.

findings.consequent: representation of a qualitative tool to be integrated with traditional quantitative methods of acoustic planning
findings.quote: The 'tender' soundmap aims also at representing a qualitative tool to be integrated with the traditional quantitative methods of the acoustic planning where the sound environment is mainly explored from a quantitative standpoint, by the means of acoustic maps.

findings.consequent: expansion of the practice of deep listening, contributing to a better overall experience in urban settings
findings.quote: Further, it is intended to expand the practice of deep listening, contributing to a better overall experience, in urban settings

findings.consequent: indication of social customs, cultural specificity, quality of life, emotions, and moods of human beings inhabiting the city
findings.quote: soundscape is indeed indicative of social customs, cultural specificity, quality of life, emotions and moods of the human beings that inhabit the city, in short, all those aspects related to the identity of a place that can not be attributed to physical forms, typologies, or numbers, and yet are no less important.

findings.consequent: interactive and open source tool, becoming a collective sound map through the involvement and participation of the Florentine population, city users and tourists
findings.quote: Finally, the “tender” soundmap is an interactive and open source tool and aims at becoming a collective sound map through the involvement and the participation of the Florentine population, city users and tourists (Radicchi, 2012).

findings.consequent: sharing of data of the 'tender' soundmap according to the UNESCO definition of Immaterial Cultural Heritage
findings.quote: since January 2013 a specific dataset called “Immaterial cultural goods” has been created within the Opendata system of the Municipality of Florence to share the data of the “tender” soundmap according to the definition of Immaterial Cultural Heritage released by UNESCO in 2003⁸.

minimum_safe_summary: This paper proposes the 'tender soundmap' of Florence, an output of a doctoral dissertation, as a tool to understand and represent urban soundscapes from an emotional standpoint, moving beyond purely cognitive approaches. Drawing on 'Emotional Geography' and 'Soundscape Studies,' the 'tender soundmap' aims to integrate qualitative analysis of the sound environment with traditional quantitative methods, promoting a 'Sensuous Urbanism' that considers the character, time, and atmospheres of places. It is envisioned as an interactive, open-source, collective sound map involving population participation to enhance and protect the Florentine urban soundscape.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: A new framework for understanding urban spaces by describing their morphology, character, time, and atmospheres, moving beyond purely cognitive approaches.
Purely cognitive approaches are insufficient for fully understanding emotional geography and soundscapes of urban spaces, necessitating a more sensuous and holistic perspective.
